t: Introduction and overview — F-4 Phantom II
name: Introduction and overview — F-4 Phantom II — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — F-4 Phantom II
description: Introduction and overview of the F-4 Phantom II: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The F-4 Phantom II is a twin-engine, two-seat fighter built by McDonnell Douglas, first flown in 1958 and the principal U.S. fighter of the Vietnam War era. A total of 5,195 were built, serving the U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force plus eleven allied nations. It set 16 world speed, altitude, and time-to-climb records. Baseline facts: Twin-engine two-seat fighter; 5,195 built by McDonnell Douglas; main U.S. fighter of the Vietnam era..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: F-4 Phantom II: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Twin-engine two-seat fighter; 5,195 built by McDonnell Douglas; main U.S. fighter of the Vietnam era.
Key figure: Top speed Mach 2.23; two General Electric J79 turbojets; 16 world performance records.
